Jordan / Lauren / Sophie — quick finance readout. We can support both approaches; here are tradeoffs and the files I attached: remit-matrix.csv (machine readable) and vat-guidance.pdf (short notes).

Option A — three invoices (recommended for AP):
- We issue INV‑NVPL‑2339‑US, INV‑NVPL‑2339‑EU, INV‑NVPL‑2339‑R&D. Each invoice will reference the PO and have its own remit_to block (bank details, entity tax ID).
- Pros: simplest for Novapulse AP & separate payment receipts; clear ledgers per legal entity.
- Cons: minor additional overhead in bookkeeping (three receivable records). We will consolidate recognition to the single contract code in RevenueOps.

Option B — single invoice with allocation lines:
- One invoice that lists three allocation rows with percent/prorated amounts and a remit matrix attached.
- Pros: single AR number internally; less clutter.
- Cons: AP systems often expect distinct invoice numbers per legal entity — reconciliation may be manual.

VAT handling: if you provide NP‑EU‑BV VAT ID, we will zero‑rate the EU invoice line if the supply is B2B and the ID validates. If no VAT ID is provided, we'll charge VAT at the local rate and include VAT breakdown per line. Please have Sophie send the EU VAT ID and company registration number.

Attachments included: remit-matrix.csv (format: invoice_number, entity_name, remit_email, bank_iban, swift, tax_id, allocation_pct), vat-guidance.pdf

If Novapulse wants our standard template, we can produce three invoices and a consolidated remit matrix within 12 business hours after we receive the EU VAT ID and remit emails. Otherwise, we can generate the single allocated invoice immediately.

Let me know which path Novapulse prefers; Sophie, if you confirm three invoices and share EU VAT ID + remit emails, we will open a ticket and push drafts for signoff.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director Finance, Redwood Inference
